text:
anika: Heads up — nightly hetero-gpu CI red on shard 7, looks like a symbol mismatch when loading libcuda on mixed A100/H100 node.
josh: Linking the job: https://ci.internal/rdw/hetero-nightly/7 — failing during model warmup, "invalid device function" then OOM cascade.
anika: Minimal log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:14Z] cuda: failed to find symbol cuGetProcAddress
[2026-03-16T03:12:14Z] kernel: launch returned invalid device function
[2026-03-16T03:12:15Z] allocator: out of memory while allocating 1.2GB
```
anika: This smells like a driver/runtime mismatch on one of the nodes in the pod — hetero nodes sometimes have one GPU with older driver layer.
lei: Which image was used? any driver pin in the node profile?
josh: Image: rdw-runtime:quant-v2 (uses CUDA 12.2 libs). Node has mixed driver versions after last infra rollout (some nodes at 515.x, some at 525.x).
michael: If cuGetProcAddress is missing it's likely older libcuda on the host. We saw this pattern when host driver < runtime lib expectation.
anika: Can we rerun this shard pinned to a nodeclass with uniform drivers? If not, can we quick-bisect which node caused the crash?
josh: I can requeue a targeted rerun to nodeclass=a100-homogenous — scheduling now. @ci-bot can you tag the rerun with debug logging and keep the node affinity?
ci-bot: Rerun scheduled by @josh: job 87421-rerun-debug -> nodeclass=a100-homogenous, env DEBUG=1. Artifacts will be kept for 7 days.
lei: Meanwhile can someone grab dmesg from the failed pod node and kubelet logs? ops-runner maybe?
ops-runner: grabbing logs now, will upload to the job artifacts. quick commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n ci get pod rdw-hetero-7 -o wide
kubectl -n ci logs rdw-hetero-7 -c runtime > /tmp/rdw-hetero-7-runtime.log
ssh gpu-node-42 sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/gpu-node-42-dmesg.txt
```
ops-runner: uploaded logs -> https://artifacts.internal/87420/hetero-7-logs.tar.gz
michael: If the rerun passes on homogeneous nodes, then it's node driver skew. If it still fails, we need to reproduce locally with same runtime+driver mix.
anika: Good plan. If rerun fails, next step: run a tiny reproducer that loads the CUDA lib and calls cuGetProcAddress on both driver versions inside a container with the runtime libs.
josh: tagging @michael for that reproducer. Can you drop a quick gist of the repro steps so I can spin it up in CI? low priority if rerun fixes it.
michael: Will do — sketching now, will post in this thread within an hour.
anika: Thanks all. I'll follow the rerun results and log attachments. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Rerun finished (87421-rerun-debug): PASSED on nodeclass=a100-homogenous. Artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/87421/hetero-7-rerun-debug.tar.gz
anika: Nice — confirms driver skew. I'll open an infra ticket to cordon nodes with older drivers and schedule a driver rollout. filing infra/driver-rollout ticket now.
lei: Add a temporary CI policy to prefer homogeneous nodeclasses for hetero-sensitive tests until rollout completes.
josh: Agreed. I'll update the pipeline to prefer nodeclass=a100-homogenous for the nightly hetero group and add a note in the release channel.
anika: Closing this thread for now — follow-up infra ticket: INFRA-1298. Ping me if reruns pop back up.
